description: SOLFORGE, Shymkent: exploring AI-powered analysis of microgravity combustion data to improve fire safety in space. Seeking teammates in coding, AI, data analysis, visualization and web development.
summary:
Flame Safety Navigator is an interactive, single-page prototype developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge: “Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data” It helps users explore how material, oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, and mission scenario relate to fire-safety research in microgravity. A schematic flame visual, educational risk tier, curated NASA research assistant, source-linked data explorer, and searchable research library bring NASA investigations—including Saffire, BASS, FLEX, SAME, and ACME—together in one accessible tool.

The project addresses the challenge by translating NASA findings and experiment resources into an approachable experience for exploring how flames behave differently in microgravity. It is important because understanding fire behavior, material flammability, and smoke detection supports safer spacecraft and future exploration. The visual and risk tier are educational only: they are not NASA measurements, a validated predictive model, or a certified safety assessment.
details:
Flame Safety Navigator is a browser-based, single-page tool for exploring NASA’s microgravity combustion research. Users select a material, oxygen setting, pressure, airflow, and mission scenario. The page updates its explanation and suggests relevant investigations. A gravity-controlled SVG flame provides a visual illustration, while a curated research assistant answers selected questions with NASA links. The Data Explorer presents supplied experiment ranges and counts, and the searchable library brings NASA and NASA PSI resources together.

The project makes complex research easier to explore and helps users see why fire behavior, material flammability, and smoke detection matter for spacecraft safety. Its intended impact is to support awareness and learning for future exploration—not to make operational safety decisions.

We built the prototype with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG. It runs in a web browser without additional hardware or a server. Our creative approach combines a visual simulator, scenario navigator, experiment facts, and research library in one experience. We prioritized responsive design, clear source links, and scientific boundaries: illustrative visuals are labeled, supplied facts are kept distinct from NASA measurements, and the risk tier is not presented as a validated NASA rating.
